summary: The floating card every anchored or modal panel is built on.

pairs.dont: Restyle the panel inside Popover, Dropdown menu or Dialog.
pairs.do: Change the surface, and let all of them move together.
pairs.why: The file says so in as many words. Four near-identical floating cards is how a system stops looking like one system.

pairs.dont: Use comfortable for a list of menu rows.
pairs.do: Compact for rows, comfortable for prose.
pairs.why: Compact's 4px padding lets a row's own padding reach the edge; comfortable's 16 gives paragraphs room.

pairs.dont: Wrap Radix's Content in a styled div.
pairs.do: Put overlaySurfaceVariants on the Content element itself.
pairs.why: Radix positions and animates that node. A wrapper leaves the shadow behind when it moves and breaks the exit animation.

pairs.dont: Rely on dimming to say something is modal.
pairs.do: Trap focus and label the panel; the scrim is decoration.
pairs.why: A screen reader never sees the dimming. What makes a dialog modal is that nothing behind it can be reached.

pairs.dont: Dim the page behind a popover or a menu.
pairs.do: Save the scrim for dialogs and drawers.
pairs.why: A scrim says "finish this first". A menu you can dismiss by looking away is not making that demand.

a11y: The scrim is aria-hidden. It is a dimming surface, not a control, and the dialog or drawer above it owns the modal semantics.
Overlay supplies no roles of its own. Everything built on it — Dialog, Drawer — brings its own Radix primitive and its own accessible name.
